title: HoBBy: Hardening Unbalanced Branches against Control Flow Attacks on Intel SGX and AMD SEV
problem: Control flow attacks (e.g., spectre, side-channel exploits) on Intel SGX and AMD SEV exploit timing differences between balanced and unbalanced branches in secret-dependent code, bypassing source-level defenses that operate only at instruction granularity.
motivation: Cryptographic and security-critical workloads on trusted execution environments (TEEs) remain vulnerable to instruction-level control flow leakage despite source-level branch balancing.
method: Compiler-based technique that identifies unbalanced instructions in secret-dependent branches via single-step analysis, then applies instruction-level transformations: shadowing (duplicate ops), cogging (interleave), and spiraling (permute) to make parallel control flows indistinguishable to attackers.
key_novelty: Instruction-level hardening of branch balancing to mask timing differences that source-level balancing misses, targeting SGX/SEV TEEs.
contributions: Single-step analysis method to identify unbalanced instructions in branches
Three instruction-level techniques (shadowing, cogging, spiraling) for control flow obfuscation
Validation against three state-of-the-art attacks on SGX and SEV
2.8% runtime overhead and 0.6% binary size overhead
baselines: three SOTA control flow attacks on SGX/SEV
limitations: Evaluation on cryptographic libraries only; generalization to other security-critical workloads, overhead on out-of-order CPUs, and interaction with speculative execution mitigations not discussed.
primary_theme: instruction-level control flow hardening for TEE cryptographic workloads
